ledger.note: 62 BC: Aretas III becomes a Roman vassal. The Aretas III page (reopened 2026-10-19): 'Despite the compliance of Aretas, in 62 BCE Scaurus marched on Petra'; the siege was lifted for 'several hundred talents of silver' and 'recognition of Roman supremacy over Nabatea'; 'Aretas would retain all Nabataean territory and possessions, becoming a vassal of the Roman Republic.' The Nabataean Kingdom page: 'The defeated Aretas paid tribute to Scaurus and recognized Roman supremacy over Nabataea.' Recorded on the vassal's side, as in boii and aetolian-league, in the lighter tint of Rome's colour; the earlier claim that the validator's pairing rule forbids it was wrong (the pair vassal_start/vassal_end with the same counterpart is all it asks). roman-republic has no mirror (it should carry vassal_start nabataeans in 62).

'In 106 AD, when Aulus Cornelius Palma Frontonianus was governor of Syria'; 'Trajan sent his army to annex the Nabataean Kingdom'. The page puts Rabbel II's death at 'early 105'; the kingdom page says he died in 106 and that two papyri from 107 AD attest the annexation. Cliopatria's row ends in 105.

wars.name: Nabataean wars with Alexander Jannaeus
wars.outcome: Jannaeus took Gaza (96) and northern Moab and Gilead; Obodas I regained them around 93 and ambushed him near Gaulane (90 on the Nabataeans page).
wars.note: The two pages disagree on the year of the victory: Battle of Gadara around 93 BC (kingdom page) against Gaulane in 90 BC (Nabataeans page).

wars.name: Tigranes II's siege of Damascus
wars.outcome: Tigranes took Damascus from Aretas III in 72; his forces were pulled out in 69 and Aretas retook the city.

wars.name: Hyrcanus II and Aristobulus II: Aretas III's siege of Jerusalem and Scaurus's march on Petra
wars.outcome: Aretas besieged Jerusalem with 50,000 men for several months for Hyrcanus II; Scaurus, bribed by Aristobulus, ordered him away, and in 62 marched on Petra; Aretas paid several hundred talents and recognised Roman supremacy.
wars.note: The page dates only Hyrcanus's accession (67) and Scaurus's march (62); the siege year is not given. No border change on these pages.

wars.name: Herod's war on Nabataea
wars.outcome: 'In 32 BC, during King Malichus I's reign, Herod the Great, with the support of Cleopatra, started a war against Nabataea'; his forces 'overran Nabataea' a year later. No territorial result on the page.

wars.name: Aretas IV's war with Herod Antipas
wars.outcome: 'Aretas invaded Herod Antipas' domain and defeated his army'; Vitellius moved south with his legions, stopping in Jerusalem 'for the passover of AD 37'.
wars.note: The page does not date Aretas' invasion; 37 is the year of the Roman response it gives, so the span is a bridging reading. Some propose Aretas briefly annexed Damascus after 37; the page says there is 'substantial evidence against Aretas controlling the city before 37 AD'.

wars.name: Roman annexation of Nabataea
wars.outcome: Trajan refused to recognise any claimant after Rabbel II's death and annexed the kingdom as Arabia Petraea (106), capital Bosra; Petra became a metropolis.

certainty.note: Desert and caravan-route frontiers, named by towns (Petra, Hegra, Bosra, Damascus, the Negev towns), never by a surveyed line; the Roman limes arabicus after 106 is outside the kingdom.

notes: Cliopatria's Nabataean shapes are the weak point: they never exceed 126k km2 and after 63 BC shrink to 90k, drawing Petra's own country (Edom) only a quarter filled and omitting Moab, the northern Negev and the Hauran. The pages opened show an intact kingdom from Petra to Hegra until 106, so every shape from -164 on is marked adjust with Edom and the Negev added (see the fix below). The Nabataeans/Nabataean Kingdom pages give no infobox area, so no area ratio could be taken. Disagreements between pages: Damascus 85-71 (kingdom page) against 85-72 and a retake in 69 (Aretas III page, used); victory over Jannaeus c. 93 (Battle of Gadara) against 90 (Gaulane); Rabbel II's death early 105 (Arabia Petraea) against 106 (kingdom page); annexation 105 (Nabataeans page body) against 106 (lead and Arabia Petraea). The seleucid-empire dossier dates a loss of 31 cells to the Nabataeans to 66 from Cliopatria alone; the Aretas III page puts Damascus in Nabataean hands from 85, so that loss should be moved to 85 and the hand-over of the Hauran/Damascus dated there. Not on the pages and therefore not in the ledger: Aelius Gallus's expedition (26-25 BC), Hegra's acquisition and Leuke Kome, Gabinius, Pompey's own settlement (the Nabataeans page gives no year for Pompey), the date Bosra came to the Nabataeans, Rabbel II's move of court. The Nabataean confederacy exists from 312/311 BC (first mention) but the map starts with the first named king. Rulers are not listed: the pages give only Aretas III (87-62), Aretas IV (c. 9 BC-AD 40), Malichus I (32 BC), Obodas I and Rabbel II (d. 105/106), not a continuous list. Gazetteer: all names used resolve ('Moab', 'Gilead', 'Edom', 'Negev', 'Hauran', 'Damascus (region)', Bosra). Page budget: 5 pages opened (plus one failed URL). [Fix 2026-10-19, after review] (1) Roman client relation recorded: vassal_start/vassal_end roman-republic 62 to 27 BC and roman-empire 27 BC to 106 (Aretas III page: Aretas 'would retain all Nabataean territory and possessions, becoming a vassal of the Roman Republic'); the vassal side is written as in boii and aetolian-league, and roman-republic still lacks its mirror (vassal_start nabataeans -62). (2) The -91 loss of the Negev and Edom to Judea is dropped (no page opened has it; the kingdom page has Obodas victorious over Jannaeus), and Edom and the Negev are carried in every keyframe from -169 so that nothing returns at -63 without an event; Judea's Cliopatria shape holds 35 Negev and 12 Edom cells from -63, so the judea dossier (me-05-f) overlaps these. (3) The -63 loss is narrowed to Damascus (Damascus page: Pompey annexed western Syria in 64, the Romans occupied Damascus); the Aretas III page says Aretas kept all his territory, so the Hauran and northern Transjordan stay Nabataean; the -27 loss of the Sinai coast is dropped (Aelius Gallus page silent), and the coast is kept in the corrected keyframes. (4) New gain from lihyan in -24 (Caskel's year; the page also gives 'around 65 BC' for the seizure of Hegra and 9 BC for Dedan); the oasis (30 cells in every Cliopatria Nabataean shape) is taken out of the keyframes before 24 and a keyframe -24..-20 puts it in. (5) Bosra: the Bosra page says 'the first Nabatean city in the 2nd century BC', so the Hauran town is Nabataean throughout. Still page-silent (confidence 1): Gilead 144, the Negev and Sinai coast 126, the 96 loss of Moab and Gilead (the Hasmonean page has Hyrcanus taking Madaba in 110), Damascus' year of loss. Aelius Gallus and Leuke Kome: the expedition landed 'at Leuke Kome in the land of the Nabataeans', undated.
